newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Germany's Kohl arrives in NZ for two-day visit.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl arrives in NZ for two-day visit.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl arrived in New Zealand on Wednesday as part of a mission to strengthen his government's links with Asia-Pacific countries and explore business opportunities.
Kohl's two-day visit is the first to New Zealand by a German chancellor. He is accompanied by a 13-member delegation of leading business representatives.

Kohl arrived in New Zealand's capital city of Wellington and is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Jim Bolger. Reserve Bank of New Zealand governor Don Brash told Reuters he would meet Kohl shortly.
Kohl will also take part in a meeting between government ministers and the German business delegation on Wednesday afternoon.
Bolger this week said he expected Kohl's visit to boost New Zealand's profile in Germany.
"We look to Germany as the anchor of economic growth and trade liberalisation in the European Union, with whom our two-way trade last year was just under $8 billion," Bolger said.

"Germany is a close diplomatic ally in areas ranging from the environment to disarmament. I expect to discuss all these areas with him. New Zealand's profile in Germany can expect to receive a significant boost as a result of the chancellor's visit."

The German government is promoting trade liberalisation in the face of opposition from its own farmers and has supported New Zealand's efforts to maintain access to the European market for its butter and sheepmeat exports.
Both nations have a strong interest in gains made during the Gatt Uruguay round on free trade.

Bolger is expected to put gentle pressure on Kohl to liberalise air services between their two countries. Germany, on the other hand, is seeking support for a permanent position on an expanded Security Council at the United Nations.
Bolger said he would also discuss political and economic reform with Kohl.
"Our MMP (Mixed Member Proportional electoral) system is based largely on the system developed in Germany. I'm certain we will exchange views," he said.

Kohl is due to meet Treasurer Winston Peters on Wednesday tonight. He will pay a social visit to a winery estate on Thursday and speak at an official dinner at Parliament that night before leaving the country.
